questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
Which statement is correct?

options.A: In the short run all factors of production are fixed; in the long run all factors are varied.
options.B: In the short run at least one factor is fixed; in the long run all factors can be varied.
options.C: In the short run at least one factor is varied; in the long run all factors are fixed.
options.D: In the short run at least one factor is varied; in the long run at least one factor is fixed.

questions.questionText: When is the supply curve for a car manufacturing firm most likely to be price elastic?

options.A: when the firm finds it difficult to recruit new labour
options.B: when the firm has a large quantity of stock
options.C: when the firm is operating in the short run
options.D: when the firm is operating near to full capacity

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect on the market for rice of a change in government policy that causes a shift in the supply curve from S to S . price S S L K J M D O quantity What does the area JKLM represent?

options.A: the cost to the government of a subsidy to rice growers

options.C: the increase in consumer surplus from the introduction of a maximum price for rice
options.D: the loss in government revenue from the reduction in a lump sum tax on rice

questions.questionText: Which statement is not an argument in support of the process of privatisation?

options.A: Private companies are motivated to make the best use of their resources.
options.B: Privatisation allows more firms to enter an industry, increasing competition in the market.
options.C: Privatisation can create companies that exploit the consumer.
options.D: Selling state-owned assets to the private sector raises significant revenue for the government.

questions.questionText: Governments are trying to reduce the burden of transfer payments in economies with an ageing population. Which policy would help to achieve this aim?

options.A: introducing financial support for university students
options.B: linking pension increases to the consumer price index during inflation
options.D: reducing state pensions to finance an equal rise in unemployment benefit

questions.questionText: Doctors are concerned about the negative health effects of sugary drinks. When would a tax on sugary drinks be least effective in improving health?

options.A: when the demand for sugary drinks is income elastic
options.B: when the demand for sugary drinks is income inelastic
options.C: when the demand for sugary drinks is price elastic
options.D: when the demand for sugary drinks is price inelastic

A country devalues its currency in the expectation that a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments will be reduced. What is necessary to make this happen?

options.C: the rate of domestic inflation is equal to the rate of inflation in the foreign market
options.D: the sum of the elasticities of demand for domestic imports and the foreign demand for exports is greater than 1
